thread.title: Nasdaq Rises Off Low; Apple Offers This Silver Lining | Investor's Business Daily

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Nasdaq Rises Off Low; Apple Offers This Silver Lining | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) fell another 2% and is desperately trying to mark a bottom as the sell-off in stocks today carried over from Tuesday's Wall Street thrashing. But thanks in part to a budding rebound in the business software sector, the Nasdaq composite trimmed its losses from more than 2% at the get-go to less than 0.4% at around 3 p.m. ET.
X The S&P 500 reflected broad selling across bank, retail, commodity and even the defensive utility sector, but it too trimmed losses to less than 1.2%. The 500 was off as much as 3% early. The Russell 2000 fell 1.3%.
In the retailing field, deep discount chain Ollie's Bargain Outlet ( OLLI ) got hammered, falling more than 17% and notching an intraday low of 70.34. The stock is testing crucial long-term support at the 200-day line as volume bulged at a pace that's running seven times its 50-day average of 676,000 shares.
The stock and longtime IBD 50 member has been a market leader for more than two years. It went public at $16 a share in 2015.
Ollie's reported excellent fiscal Q3 results as earnings jumped 45% to 32 cents a share on a 19% bump up in sales.
The U.S. Services Sector Is Still Growing Meanwhile, the Institute for Supply Management reported a boost in its services sector index in November to 60.7, blasting the Econoday consensus estimate of 59.0 and rising from an October reading of 60.3. The increase suggests that service sectors in the U.S. continue to enjoy expanding business. A reading above 50 indicates industry expansion.
The Dow Jones industrial average slumped nearly 2% as at least a dozen of the 30 components within the blue chip average dropped 2 points or more. But amid Chinese furor over the arrest of Huawei Technologies' CFO, some non-Chinese telecom gear firms rallied or kept losses mild. They included Ciena ( CIEN ), a specialist in fiber optic broadband equipment and a current member of IBD Leaderboard.
Shares in Ciena rallied nearly 1% but remain below a 32.43 correct buy point in a newly formed base, a nine-week cup without handle .
Volume was running higher vs. the same time on Tuesday for both main exchanges. Wall Street was closed Wednesday in honor of the late President George H.W. Bush.
Some Megacap Techs Defy The Sell-Off Cisco Systems ( CSCO ), one of the better performers in the Dow lately, traded virtually flat. It boasts an 88 Relative Price Strength Rating on a scale of 1 to 99, as seen in IBD Stock Checkup .
Cisco, which was the best growth stock in the 1990s due to its excellence in the data router and switch, has become a serious force in telecommunications equipment as well. Like Apple, the San Jose, Calif., firm has staged a steady turnaround in its fundamentals.
Earnings have grown 11%, 10%, 15% and 23% vs. year-ago levels in the past four quarters. The Street sees earnings lifting another 14% to 72 cents a share in the January-ending fiscal second quarter.
Cisco's SMR Rating, which tracks sales, profit margins and return on equity, is a sterling A.
The stock is forming a flat base with a 49.57 proper entry point . That base began to form after Cisco cleared a 46.47 buy point in a longer flat-base pattern in late August in quiet turnover.
Meanwhile, keep an eye on potential new breakouts and the continuation of long-term price uptrends among up-and-coming leaders in the enterprise, database and security software industries.
Young Turks In The Software Realm Twilio ( TWLO ), ServiceNow ( NOW ), Trade Desk ( TTD ) and Atlassian ( TEAM ) are now showing increasing relative strength vs. the S&P 500. Watch the slope of a stock's relative strength line. A rising line means either a stock is rising faster than the S&P 500, or falling less intensely.
Atlassian and ServiceNow are current members of the seven-stock IBD Sector Leaders top stock list .
Even a pair of profitless software firms, Okta ( OKTA ) and MongoDB ( MDB ), etched solid gains. Both companies are expected to post a loss for fiscal 2018, but network security specialist Okta harbors excellent operating cash flow.
MongoDB has shown superb sales growth that has exceeded 50% on a year-over-year basis in eight of the past nine quarters. But the Street expects the company to lose $1.55 a share in fiscal 2019, which ends in January.
Once A Nasdaq Star Stock, Apple Is Still Under Pressure Apple has now corrected more than 23% from a peak of 233.47. That's still slimmer than the 33% correction witnessed during a battleship-long base that formed from May 2015 to May 2016.
The current decline, prompted again by lingering concern over holiday-quarter iPhone sales, actually provides a silver lining for the once largest company in U.S. financial markets by market cap. That is, Apple is going through a needed flushing out of less-committed holders.
The stock also undercut the 180.73 low of a flat base that formed from June to July. This means the base count resets .
In Other Financial Markets Crude oil got battered as U.S. futures dropped more than 3% to $51.15 a barrel. Crude has now plunged more than 33% below a 52-week high near $75.
Investors continued to stream into long-dated U.S. Treasuries. The benchmark yield on the 10-year bond sank to 2.85%.
